messages:
alexa: Quick heads-up: proposing an RBAC tweak for private/on‑prem customers. New role 'emergency-operator' to allow one-off maintenance ops (jumpbox only). Need comments on network controls + keystore attestation requirements.
peter: Can you outline the intended privileges?
alexa: Read-only controlplane + decrypt grant for a scoped KMS key for 30s per session. Token minted only after an attestation handshake from the on-prem keystore-proxy. No long-lived keys.
ravi: Sounds good. Two concerns: 1) DNS leakage when ops use the bastion for lookups, 2) ensuring the attestation proof cannot be replayed.
tia: On DNS: enforce split-horizon and egress allowlist. Our suggestion: create a VPC-only DNS resolver via VPC endpoint and restrict bastion/nodes to only talk to that. For kubernetes, default deny egress for all non-proxy pods.
alexa: For attestation replay: require a nonce from control plane when attestation initiated, tie to ephemeral session id and require attestation TTL < 60s. Store only HMAC of attestation in audit logs.
peter: Forensics and audit: we should forward structured metadata to customer's SIEM (timestamp, actor, session_id, attestation_hmac, decrypt_request_id). Redact any request/response payloads. Also sign exported bundles with our export key.
ravi: Triage note: there's a reported kernel eBPF flaw that could allow local actors to bypass netfilter (CVE-2026-0420). If unpatched, bastion eBPF-based L7 filters are risky. Fallback: rely on iptables netpol + dedicated DNS proxy container.
tia: Agreed. Also recommend enabling user namespaces for jumpbox containers and set seccomp + no-new-privs. Drop CAP_SYS_ADMIN and CAP_NET_ADMIN.
alexa: Incident playbook draft: 1) auto-suspend emergency-operator grants if attestation anomalies detected, 2) snapshot keystore-proxy logs + DNS proxy logs, 3) isolate bastion network, 4) rotate KMS grant and issue scoped emergency key, 5) start forensics capture (pcap) for impacted subnets for 48h (customer consent required).
sec-bot: [automated] alert: attestation mismatch for svc:emergency-operator at 1700011255  check:nonce_mismatch count=3 link=https://inc/RED-2001
peter: On that alert, block signing requests immediately, switch proxy to maintenance mode and spin denylist for the session id. Who owns the runbook?
tia: I'll take runbook ownership. Will add steps to notify customer security contacts and legal if any data-plane decrypts occur outside sessions.
ravi: NetworkPolicy snippet for bastion pods (allow only DNS resolver + keystore proxy):
```
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: bastion-tight-egress
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      role: bastion
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.240.0.0/16
      ports:
      - protocol: UDP
        port: 53
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          app: keystore-proxy
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
```
alexa: Nice. Retention: default on-prem audit retention 90 days, opt-in up to 2 years for regulated customers. All exported logs must include per-record HMAC and be immutable once written.
peter: One more: we should require customer opt-in for pcap collection and provide a signed tamper-evidence manifest.
alexa: Good call. I'll open the RBAC PR and include these network + attestation constraints, tag @tia for runbook edits and @ravi for vuln mitigations. Thanks all.
